groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
M: It's my last day at work tomorrow. I'll start my new job in two weeks. My human resources manager wants to conduct an interview with me before I leave.
W: Ah, an exit interview. Are you looking forward to it?
M: I'm not sure how I feel about it. I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time, but I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel.
W: To my way of thinking, there are two main potential benefits that come from unleashing an agitated stream of truth during an exit interview. The first is release. Unburdening yourself of frustration, and perhaps even anger to someone who isn't a friend or close colleague can be wonderfully freeing.
M: And let me guess. The second is that the criticism will, theoretically, help the organization I'm leaving to improve, making sure employees of the future are less likely to encounter what I did?
W: That's right. But the problem with the company improvement part is that very often it doesn't happen. An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't. In my company, the information gained from these interviews is often not confidential. And the information is used as dirt against another manager, or can be traded among senior managers.
M: Now you've got me rethinking what I'll disclose in the interview. There is always a chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry. It is a pretty small industry after all.
W: Anything you initially gain from the instant satisfaction of telling it like it is, you might lose down the track by injuring your future career prospects.
M: Right. Perhaps it would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate-your-employer websites.
W: You could. And don't do the interview at all. Exit interviews are not mandatory.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
M: Today, I'm talking to the renowned botanist, Jane Forster.
W: Thank you for inviting me to join you on the show, Henry.
M: Recently, Jane, you've become quite a celebrity since the release of your latest documentary. Can you tell us a little about it?
W: Well, it follows my expedition to study the vegetation indigenous to the rainforest in equatorial areas of Southeast Asia.
M: You certainly get to travel to some very exotic locations.
W: It was far from glamorous, to be honest. The area we visited was accessible only by canoe and the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least. There was no electricity. And our water supply was a nearby stream.
M: How were the weather conditions while you were there?
W: The weather was not conducive to our work at all, since the humidity was almost unbearable. At midday, we stayed in the hut and did nothing. It was too humid to either work or sleep.
M: How long did your team spend in the jungle?
W: Originally, we planned to be there for a month. But in the end, we stayed for only two weeks.
M: Why did you cut the expedition short?
W: Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching. And we had to evacuate at very short notice.
M: That sounds like a fascinating anecdote.
W: It was frightening. The fastest evacuation route was through river rapids. We had to navigate them carrying all of our equipment.
M: So overall, was the journey unsuccessful?
W: Absolutely not. We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life.
M: Why do you put up with such adverse conditions?
W: Botany is an obsession for me. Many of the destinations I visit have stunning scenery. And I get to meet a variety of people from all over the world.
M: So where will your next destination be?
W: I haven't decided yet.
M: Then we can leave it for another occasion. Thanks.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Scientists often use specialized jargon terms while communicating with laymen. Most of them don't realize the harmful effects of this practice. In a new study, people exposed to jargon when reading about subjects like autonomous vehicles and surgical robots later said they were less interested in science than others who read about the same topics, but without the use of specialized terms. They also felt less informed about science and less qualified to discuss science topics. It's noteworthy that it made no difference if the jargon terms were defined in the text. Even when the terms were defined, readers still felt the same lack of engagement as readers who read jargon that wasn't explained.
The problem is that the mere presence of jargon sends a discouraging message to readers. Hillary Schulman, the author of the study, asserts that specialized words are a signal. Jargon tells people that the message isn't for them.
There's an even darker side to how people react to jargon. In another study, researchers found that reading scientific articles containing jargon led people to doubt the actual science. They found the opposite when a text is easier to read. Then people are more persuaded.
Thus, it's important to communicate clearly when talking about complex science subjects. This is especially true with issues related to public health, like the safety of new medications and the benefits of vaccines. Schulman concedes that the use of jargon is appropriate with scientific audiences. But scientists who want to communicate with the general public need to modify their language. They need to eliminate jargon.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
At the beginning of the twentieth century, on the Gulf Coast in the US state of Texas, there was a hill where gas leakage was so noticeable that schoolboys would sometimes set the hill on fire.
Pattillo Higgins, a disreputable local businessman, became convinced that there was oil below the gassy hill. Oil wells weren't drilled back then; they were essentially dug. The sand under the hill defeated several attempts by Higgins' workers to make a proper hole. Higgins had forecast oil at 1,000 feet, a totally made-up figure.
Higgins subsequently hired a mining engineer, Captain Anthony Lucas. After encountering several setbacks, Captain Lucas decided to use a drill, and his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry.
In January 1901, at 1,020 feet-almost precisely the depth predicted by Higgins' wild guess—the well roared and suddenly ejected mud and six tons of drilling pipe out of the ground, terrifying those present. For the next nine days, until the well was capped, the well poured out more oil than all the wells in America combined.
In those days, Texas was almost entirely rural, with no large cities and practically no industry; cotton and beef were the foundation of the economy. Higgins' well changed that. The boom made some prospectors millionaires, but the sudden surplus of petroleum was not entirely a blessing for Texas. In the 1930s, prices crashed, to the point that in some parts of the country oil was cheaper than water. That would become a familiar pattern of the boom-or-bust Texas' economy.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Most people dislike their jobs. It's an astonishing but statistical fact. A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that many believe they have terrible managers. Few describe their managers as malicious or manipulative though. While those types certainly exist, they are a minority. The majority of managers, seemingly, just don't know any better. They are often emulating bad managers they've had in the past. It's likely they've never read a management book or attended a management course. They might not have even reflected on what good management looks like and how it would influence their own management style.
The researchers interviewed employees about their managers, beginning with a question about the worst manager they had ever had. From this, the researchers came up with four main causes of why some managers are perceived as being simply awful at their jobs.
The first cause was company culture, which was seen by employees as enabling poor management practices. It was specifically stressful work environments, minimal training and a lack of accountability that were found to be the most blameworthy. Often a manager's superiors can effectively encourage a manager's distasteful behavior when they fail to discipline the person's wrongdoings. Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic.
The second cause was attributed to the managers' characteristics. Those deemed to be most destructive were odd people—those without drive, those who allow personal problems into the workplace, and those with an unpleasant temperament or personality in general.
The third cause of poor management was associated with a deficiency of qualifications not so much the formal variety one obtains from a university, but the informal variety that comes from credible work experience and professional accomplishments.
The fourth cause concerned managers who've been promoted for reasons other than potential. One reason in particular why these people had been promoted was that they had been around the longest. It wasn't their skill set or other merits that got them the job; it was their tenure.
A point worth making is that the study was based only on the perspective of employees. The researchers didn't ask senior leaders what they thought of their frontline managers. It's quite possible they're content with how the individuals they promoted are now performing, merrily ignorant of the damage they're actually causing, which might explain why, as the researchers conclude, those same middle managers are usually unaware that they are a bad manager.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
With the use of driverless vehicles seemingly inevitable, mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are definitely taking the lead.
Iron ore is a key ingredient in steel-making. The mining companies here produce almost 300 million tons of iron ore a year. The 240 giant autonomous trucks in use, in the Western Australian mines, can weigh 400 tons, fully loaded, and travel at speeds of up to 60 kilometers per hour. They are a technological leap, transporting iron ore along routes which run for hundreds of kilometers from mines to their destinations. Here when the truck arrives at its destination, staff in the operation center direct it precisely where to unload. Vast quantities of iron ore are then transported by autonomous trains to ocean ports.
Advocates argue these automated vehicles will change mining forever. It may only be five years before the use of automation technology leads to a fully robotic mine.
A range of factors has pushed Western Australia's desert region to the lead of this automation revolution. These include the huge size of the mines, the scale of equipment and the repetitive nature of some of the work. Then there's the area's remoteness. At 502,000 square kilometers, it can sometimes make recruiting staff a challenge. Another consideration is the risks when humans interact with large machinery. There are also the financial imperatives. The ongoing push by the mining corporations to be more productive and more efficient is another powerful driver in embracing automation technology.
The concept of a fully autonomous mine is a bit of a misleading term, however. This is because the more technology is put into the field, the more people are needed to deploy, maintain and improve it.
The automation and digitization of the industry are creating a need for different jobs. These include data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence. The mining companies claim automation and robotics present opportunities to make mining more sustainable and safer. Employees will be offered a career that is even more fulfilling and more rewarding.
Workers' unions have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology. But they still have reservations about the rise of automation technology. Their main concern is the potential impact on remote communities. As automation spreads further, the question is how these remote communities will survive when the old jobs are eliminated. And this may well prove to be the most significant impact of robotic technology in many places around the world.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
According to official statistics, Thailand's annual road-death rate is almost double the global average. Thai people know that their roads are dangerous, but they don't know this could easily be changed.
Globally, road accidents kill more people every year than any infectious disease. Researchers at the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in America put the death toll in 2017 at 1.24 million. According to the institute, the overall number of deaths has been more or less static since the turn of the century. But that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries.
In many poor countries, road accidents are killing more people than ever before. Those countries have swelling, young populations, a fast-growing fleet of cars and motorbikes, and a limited supply of surgeons. It is impossible to know for sure because official statistics are so inadequate, but deaths are thought to have risen by 40% since 1990 in many low-income countries. In many rich countries, by contrast, roads are becoming even safer. In Estonia and Ireland, for example, the number of deaths has fallen by about two-thirds since the late 1990s.
But the most important and intriguing changes are taking place in middle-income countries, which contain most of the world's people and have some of the most dangerous roads. According to researchers, in China and South Africa, traffic deaths have been falling since 2000, and in India since 2012, and the Philippines reached its peak four years ago. The question is whether Thailand can soon follow suit.
Rob MeInerney, head of the International Road Assessment Programme, says that all countries tend to go through three phases. They begin with poor, slow roads. In the second phase, as they grow wealthier, they pave the roads, allowing traffic to move faster and pushing up the death rate. Lastly, in the third phase, countries act to make their roads safer. The trick, then, is to reach the third stage sooner, by focusing earlier and more closely on fatal accidents.
How to do that? The solution lies not just in better infrastructure, but in better social incentives. Safe driving habits are practices which people know they should follow but often don't. Dangerous driving is not a fixed cultural trait, as some imagine. People respond to incentives, such as traffic laws that are actually enforced.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
options: He will tell the management how he really feels.
He will meet his new manager in two weeks.
He is going to attend a job interview.
He is going to leave his present job.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the man from the conversation? 

 【翻译】 从对话中我们了解到这个男士的什么情况? 
 A)  他会告诉管理层他的真实感受。 
 B)  他将在两周后见他的新经理。 
 C)  他将要参加一个工作面试。 
 D)  他将要离开他现在的工作。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） He is going to leave his present job. 
 【定位】 P3 I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time. 
 我辞职了，因为我在那家公司已经不开心很久了。 

 【信号】 被问者自述 I resigned 的直接陈述 。男士开口第一段就说 It's my last day at work tomorrow. I'll start my new job in two weeks.，到第三段又点明 I resigned because I've been unhappy at that company for a long time。『resigned』『last day』『new job』几个自述合起来，明确他要离开现职——这是说话人自己交代现状的直接信号。 

 【替换】 I resigned ↔ leave his present job resign 等于 leave the job 
 It's my last day at work tomorrow. ↔ leave his present job 明天最后一天即将离职 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项盗用了 tell them how I really feel 这串原词，但男士说的是 I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel（不确定该不该说），是犹豫，不是『他将会说』。把『不确定要不要』听成『他会』，正中圈套。  借用原文：I'm not sure if I should tell them how I really feel 

 B) 原词陷阱 选项偷用了 in two weeks 这个时间词，但原文是 I'll start my new job in two weeks（两周后开始新工作），根本没提『见新经理』。听到 two weeks 就选 B，是被数字原词牵着走。  借用原文：I'll start my new job in two weeks 

 C) 偷换概念 选项借了原文反复出现的 interview 一词，但原文的 conduct an interview with me before I leave 和 an exit interview 是『离职面谈』，而非 a job interview（求职面试）。同一个 interview，性质完全不同。  借用原文：an exit interview

questions.prompt: What does the woman think about the information gained from an exit interview?
options: It should be kept private.
It should be carefully analyzed.
It can be quite useful to senior managers.
It can improve interviewees' job prospects.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman think about the information gained from an exit interview? 

 【翻译】 女士对从离职面谈中获得的信息有什么看法? 
 A)  应该保密。 
 B)  应该仔细分析。 
 C)  对高层管理者来说可能相当有用。 
 D)  可以改善面试者的工作前景。 

 【答案】 A （态度观点题） It should be kept private. 
 【定位】 P6 An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't. In my company, the information gained from these interviews is often not confidential. 
 离职面谈本应是保密的，但常常并非如此。在我公司，这些面谈得到的信息往往并不保密。 

 【信号】 supposed to be 表『本应当』的主张 。女士说 An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn't，be supposed to 表示『理应、本该』，正是她对这信息该如何的主张：本该保密。后半 but often isn't 是补充现实，但她持的立场仍是『应当保密』。 

 【替换】 supposed to be private ↔ It should be kept private supposed to be 等于 should be 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 选项 carefully analyzed 在录音里找不到对应说法，女士谈的是保密与被滥用，没有提到『仔细分析』。这是凭空添加的内容。 
 C) 原词陷阱 选项盗用了 senior managers 这个原词，但原文是 traded among senior managers（在高管间被当把柄交易），是负面滥用，而非 useful to senior managers（对高管有用）这种正面评价。听到 senior managers 就选，正中陷阱。  借用原文：can be traded among senior managers 

 D) 与原文相反 选项 improve interviewees' job prospects（改善求职前景）与原文方向相反：录音第8段说乱说话会 injuring your future career prospects（损害前途），是变坏不是变好。极性被反转了。  借用原文：injuring your future career prospects
questions.spoken_text: What does the woman think about the information gained from an exit interview?

questions.prompt: Why does the man want to rethink what he will say in the coming exit interview?
options: It may leave a negative impression on the interviewer.
It may adversely affect his future career prospects.
It may displease his immediate superiors.
It may do harm to his fellow employees.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the man want to rethink what he will say in the coming exit interview? 

 【翻译】 男士为什么想要重新考虑他在即将进行的离职面谈中要说的话? 
 A)  可能会给面试官留下负面印象。 
 B)  可能会对他未来的职业前景产生不利影响。 
 C)  可能会让他的直属上级不高兴。 
 D)  可能会对他的同事造成伤害。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It may adversely affect his future career prospects. 
 【定位】 P7 There is always a chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry. 
 总有一种可能，它会影响我的声誉和我在行业里建立人脉的能力。 

 【信号】 it could affect 表担忧的因果句 。男士说 Now you've got me rethinking what I'll disclose，紧接 There is always a chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry。could affect 点出他改主意的原因——怕影响声誉和人脉；下一段女士又用 injuring your future career prospects 把这归结为『损害未来职业前景』，因果信号明确。 

 【替换】 affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry ↔ adversely affect his future career prospects 声誉人脉受损概括为前途受损 
 injuring your future career prospects ↔ adversely affect his future career prospects injure 等于 adversely affect 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 选项 negative impression on the interviewer 借了话题里的 interview 氛围，但男士担心的是声誉和人脉、行业里的名声，从没提『给面试官留下负面印象』。这是没有依据的添加。 
 C) 张冠李戴 选项盗用了第6段 dirt against another manager 的 manager 语境，但那是女士讲『信息被用来对付别的经理』，并非男士改主意是怕惹自己的顶头上司。把别处的内容嫁接到本题原因上，是张冠李戴。  借用原文：used as dirt against another manager 

 D) 未提及 选项 harm to his fellow employees 在录音里找不到对应：男士担心的是自己的前途，女士谈的是信息被高管滥用，谁都没说会伤到同事。这是凭空捏造的受害对象。
questions.spoken_text: Why does the man want to rethink what he will say in the coming exit interview?

questions.prompt: What does the man think he had better do?
options: Prepare a comprehensive exit report.
Do some practice for the exit interview.
Network with his close friends to find a better employer.
Pour out his frustrations on a rate-your-employer website.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man think he had better do? 

 【翻译】 男士认为他最好做什么? 
 A)  准备一份全面的离职报告。 
 B)  为离职面谈做一些练习。 
 C)  与他的密友建立联系以找到更好的雇主。 
 D)  在雇主评价网站上发泄他的不满。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Pour out his frustrations on a rate-your-employer website. 
 【定位】 P9 Perhaps it would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate-your-employer websites. 
 也许更好的办法是去那些给雇主打分的网站上把心里话一吐为快。 

 【信号】 Perhaps it would be better 表打算的建议句 。对话临近结尾，男士说 Perhaps it would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate-your-employer websites。it would be better 直接表达他认为更好的做法，正是题干『had better do』要找的打算句，出现在对话后半段，符合建议常落尾部的规律。 

 【替换】 getting things off my chest ↔ Pour out his frustrations get off chest 等于 pour out frustrations 
 going to one of those rate-your-employer websites ↔ on a rate-your-employer website 同一渠道名几乎原样对应 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 选项 Prepare a comprehensive exit report 借了话题里的 exit 一词，造出『写一份详尽的离职报告』，但录音里男士从没说要写报告。这是凭空添加的方案。 
 B) 原词陷阱 选项 Do some practice for the exit interview 盗用了 exit interview 这一原词，但全程没有任何人提到『为面谈做练习』；女士最后反而说 don't do the interview at all（干脆别做这面谈）。听到 exit interview 就选，正中原词陷阱。  借用原文：don't do the interview at all 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 Network with his close friends to find a better employer 借了第7段 network in the industry 的 network 一词，但原文的 network 是『在行业建人脉』且是怕受损，并非『找好友另找雇主』。盗 network 来拼错意，是原词陷阱。  借用原文：my ability to network in the industry

questions.prompt: What does the man want Jane Forster to talk about?
options: Her unsuccessful journey.
Her month-long expedition.
Her latest documentary.
Her career as a botanist.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man want Jane Forster to talk about? 

 【翻译】 男士想让Jane Forster谈论什么? 
 A)  她不成功的旅程。 
 B)  她为期一个月的考察。 
 C)  她最新的纪录片。 
 D)  她作为植物学家的职业生涯。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Her latest documentary. 
 【定位】 P3 Recently, Jane, you've become quite a celebrity since the release of your latest documentary. Can you tell us a little about it? 
 简，最近你随着最新纪录片的发行成了名人。你能跟我们聊聊它吗？ 

 【信号】 主持人的直接请求句 。信号是主持人发出的请求 Can you tell us a little about it?，其中 it 回指上一句的 your latest documentary——一问一请求，正是他想让她谈的对象，答案就落在这句。 

 【替换】 your latest documentary ↔ Her latest documentary. 近乎原词对应 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 unsuccessful journey 借了对话后段主持人那句 was the journey unsuccessful? 的原词，但那是结尾另一问，并非开场主持人请她谈的话题，听到 unsuccessful/journey 就选属于答非所问。  借用原文：was the journey unsuccessful? 

 B) 原词陷阱 month-long expedition 借了她回答里 my expedition 与 planned to be there for a month 的原词拼成，但主持人开场请她谈的是纪录片本身，不是"为期一月的远征"这件事，属答非所问。  借用原文：my expedition 

 D) 原词陷阱 career as a botanist 借了开场 the renowned botanist 的原词，但主持人没有请她谈"植物学家的职业生涯"，只请她谈纪录片，听到 botanist 就选属答非所问。  借用原文：the renowned botanist
questions.spoken_text: What does the man want Jane Forrester to talk about?

questions.prompt: Why does the woman describe her experience as "far from glamorous"?
options: She had to live like a vegetarian.
She was caught in a hurricane.
She had to endure many hardships.
She suffered from water shortage.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the woman describe her experience as "far from glamorous"? 

 【翻译】 女士为什么把她的经历描述为"远非光鲜亮丽"? 
 A)  她不得不像素食者一样生活。 
 B)  她遭遇了飓风。 
 C)  她不得不忍受许多艰难困苦。 
 D)  她遭受了缺水之苦。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） She had to endure many hardships. 
 【定位】 P6 It was far from glamorous, to be honest. The area we visited was accessible only by canoe and the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least. There was no electricity. And our water supply was a nearby stream. 
 老实说，那远谈不上光鲜。我们去的地方只能靠独木舟进入，小屋里的居住条件说轻点也是非常原始的。没有电。我们的水源就是附近一条小溪。 

 【信号】 原话之后的连串列举 。信号是她说完 far from glamorous 后一口气列举多重恶劣条件：accessible only by canoe、living conditions in the hut were primitive、no electricity、water supply was a nearby stream。连珠炮式的多项困难，正是答案句。 

 【替换】 the living conditions in the hut were primitive ↔ She had to endure many hardships. 多项困难概括为吃苦 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 live like a vegetarian（像素食者一样生活）极易与录音里 the vegetation indigenous to the rainforest 的 vegetation 听混，但 vegetation 是"植被"、vegetarian 是"素食者"，原文从未说她被迫吃素，属听音致误的相近词陷阱。  借用原文：the vegetation indigenous to the rainforest 

 B) 原词陷阱 caught in a hurricane 借了后文 a hurricane was approaching 的原词，但飓风是导致提前结束（第 7 题）的原因，并非她说 far from glamorous 的缘由，张冠李戴到本题。  借用原文：a hurricane was approaching 

 D) 偷换概念 water shortage（缺水）盗用了 our water supply was a nearby stream 里的 water，但原文是说"水源是条小溪"（条件简陋），并非缺水；且只取一样困难，与"many hardships"的总括不符。  借用原文：our water supply was a nearby stream

questions.prompt: Why did the woman and those who went with her end their trip halfway?
options: A hurricane was coming.
A flood was approaching.
They had no more food in the canoe.
They could no longer bear the humidity.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why did the woman and those who went with her end their trip halfway? 

 【翻译】 女士和与她同行的人为什么中途结束了旅程? 
 A)  飓风即将来临。 
 B)  洪水正在逼近。 
 C)  他们的独木舟里没有食物了。 
 D)  他们无法再忍受湿度了。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） A hurricane was coming. 
 【定位】 P12 Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching. And we had to evacuate at very short notice. 
 行程过半时，我们收到飓风正在逼近的消息。我们不得不在极短时间内撤离。 

 【信号】 received news that + had to 因果链 。信号是 we received news that a hurricane was approaching 接着 we had to evacuate——"得知飓风逼近"是因、"被迫撤离"是果，had to 的被迫语气坐实了这就是提前结束的原因句。 

 【替换】 a hurricane was approaching ↔ A hurricane was coming. approaching 同义于 coming 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 flood（洪水）在录音里从未出现，它借了后文 river rapids（激流）造成的"和水有关"的联想，但原文撤离原因是飓风不是洪水，属凭联想编造的未提及项。 
 C) 原词陷阱 no more food in the canoe 借了 accessible only by canoe 的 canoe，但原文从没提食物耗尽，独木舟是"进出方式"而非"断粮地点"，听到 canoe 就选属原词陷阱。  借用原文：accessible only by canoe 

 D) 原词陷阱 no longer bear the humidity 借了 the humidity was almost unbearable 的 humidity，但潮湿是描述天气难受（第 6/8 题背景），不是中途撤离的原因——撤离是因飓风，张冠李戴到本题。  借用原文：the humidity was almost unbearable

questions.prompt: What does the woman think of the journey?
options: It was memorable.
It was unbearable.
It was uneventful.
It was fruitful.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman think of the journey? 

 【翻译】 女士如何看待这次旅程? 
 A)  令人难忘的。 
 B)  难以忍受的。 
 C)  平淡无奇的。 
 D)  富有成果的。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） It was fruitful. 
 【定位】 P16 Absolutely not. We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life. 
 绝对不是。我们采集了关于当地植物的海量数据。 

 【信号】 强烈否定 + 反转后的正向定调 。信号是主持人问 was the journey unsuccessful?（负面设问），她以 Absolutely not. 强烈否定反转，再用 gathered a massive amount of data 给出正向定调——"不是失败、收获巨大"才是她的真实态度。 

 【替换】 We gathered a massive amount of data ↔ It was fruitful. 采集海量数据等于有收获 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 memorable（难忘）听上去是正面评价，像能套上整段经历，但她对行程的总评落点是"有收获"，原文并未说"难忘"，属凭褒义氛围误推、原文未提及的态度。 
 B) 与原文相反 unbearable 盗自 the humidity was almost unbearable，那是形容潮湿天气难忍，并非她对整段 journey 的评价；况且她明确否定行程失败，态度是正面，与 unbearable 相反。  借用原文：the humidity was almost unbearable 

 C) 与原文相反 uneventful（平淡无事）与原文截然相反——她经历了飓风逼近、紧急撤离、激流行船，行程绝非平淡，这是把惊险经历反说成平淡的反向干扰。  借用原文：It was frightening.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the use of jargon terms by experts?
options: It diminishes laymen's interest in science.
It ensures the accuracy of their arguments.
It makes their expressions more explicit.
It hurts laymen's dignity and self-esteem.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about the use of jargon terms by experts? 

 【翻译】 文章关于专家使用术语说了什么? 
 A)  它削弱了外行人对科学的兴趣。 
 B)  它确保了他们论证的准确性。 
 C)  它使他们的表达更加明确。 
 D)  它伤害了外行人的尊严和自尊。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It diminishes laymen's interest in science. 
 【定位】 P1 Most of them don't realize the harmful effects of this practice. In a new study, people exposed to jargon when reading about subjects like autonomous vehicles and surgical robots later said they were less interested in science than others who read about the same topics, but without the use of specialized terms. 
 他们大多数人没意识到这种做法的有害影响。在一项新研究中，阅读自动驾驶汽车、手术机器人等话题时接触到术语的人，事后表示自己对科学的兴趣低于那些读同样话题但没用专业术语的人。 

 【信号】 定性词harmful＋对比 。答案句的信号是定性词 the harmful effects（有害影响）和紧随其后的对比结果 less interested in science：录音先给出"有害"的定性，再用接触术语者 vs 未接触者的对照坐实是哪种害处，这两处合起来就是答案落点。 

 【替换】 less interested in science ↔ diminishes laymen's interest in science 形容词改写为动词 
 people exposed to jargon ↔ laymen's interest people＝laymen 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 盗用了术语话题里反复出现的 science 一词，编出 ensures the accuracy of their arguments.（确保论点准确）。但原文只说术语"有害"、让人兴趣下降，从未说它"确保准确"，方向正相反，是听到 science 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：less interested in science 

 C) 与原文相反 C 说术语 makes their expressions more explicit.（使表达更清晰），是正面作用；但原文定性是 the harmful effects，且第 2 段说术语 sends a discouraging message，方向与 C 完全相反，属与原文相反的干扰。  借用原文：the harmful effects of this practice 

 D) 未提及 D 说术语 hurts laymen's dignity and self-esteem.（伤害外行尊严与自尊）。原文确实讲了多种负面后果——兴趣下降、感觉 less informed、less qualified to discuss，但从未提"尊严/自尊"，dignity、self-esteem 是原文没出现的概念，属未提及。

questions.prompt: What do researchers find about people reading scientific articles containing jargon terms?
options: They can learn to communicate with scientists.
They tend to disbelieve the actual science.
They feel great respect towards scientists.
They will see the complexity of science.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do researchers find about people reading scientific articles containing jargon terms? 

 【翻译】 研究人员关于人们阅读含有术语的科学文章发现了什么? 
 A)  他们可以学会与科学家交流。 
 B)  他们倾向于不相信真正的科学。 
 C)  他们对科学家感到非常尊敬。 
 D)  他们会看到科学的复杂性。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They tend to disbelieve the actual science. 
 【定位】 P3 In another study, researchers found that reading scientific articles containing jargon led people to doubt the actual science. They found the opposite when a text is easier to read. 
 在另一项研究中，研究者发现，阅读含有术语的科学文章会让人怀疑真实的科学。而当文章更易读时，他们发现的结果正相反。 

 【信号】 研究发现动词＋后续转折 。信号是 researchers found that（研究者发现）这个直接报告发现的动词，题干 find 与它对应；其后还有 They found the opposite when a text is easier to read. 的对比，进一步把"含术语→怀疑"这一发现衬得更实。听到 researchers found 就锁定这句。 

 【替换】 led people to doubt the actual science ↔ They tend to disbelieve the actual science. doubt＝disbelieve 
 reading scientific articles containing jargon led people ↔ They people＝They 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 A 说他们 can learn to communicate with scientists.，借用了全篇关于"沟通"的话题氛围（如 communicating with laymen），但原文讲的是读者"怀疑科学"，从没说读者会"学会与科学家沟通"，属答非所问。  借用原文：communicating with laymen 

 C) 与原文相反 C 说他们 feel great respect towards scientists.（对科学家更敬重），是正面反应；但原文是 doubt the actual science（怀疑科学），方向相反。读术语文章让人更不信、而非更敬重，属与原文相反。  借用原文：led people to doubt the actual science 

 D) 过度推断 D 说他们 will see the complexity of science.（会看到科学的复杂），蹭了第 4 段 complex science subjects 的 complex 一词，听着"合理"。但答案句说的是"怀疑科学"，不是"看到科学复杂"，原文未就读者得出"看到复杂性"这一发现，属过度推断。  借用原文：complex science subjects

questions.prompt: What does Schulman suggest scientists do when communicating with the general public?
options: Find appropriate topics.
Stimulate their interest.
Explain all the jargon terms.
Do away with jargon terms.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does Schulman suggest scientists do when communicating with the general public? 

 【翻译】 Schulman建议科学家在与公众交流时做什么? 
 A)  找到合适的话题。 
 B)  激发他们的兴趣。 
 C)  解释所有的术语。 
 D)  摒弃术语。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Do away with jargon terms. 
 【定位】 P4 But scientists who want to communicate with the general public need to modify their language. They need to eliminate jargon. 
 但想与普通大众沟通的科学家需要调整自己的语言。他们需要去掉术语。 

 【信号】 转折But＋建议need to 。双重信号：先是转折 But（前句说术语对专业听众尚可，But 后才是对大众的真正主张），再是建议动词 need to eliminate jargon。转折后＋need to 之处，正是对策题答案落点。 

 【替换】 eliminate jargon ↔ Do away with jargon terms. eliminate＝do away with 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 说要 Find appropriate topics.（找合适话题）。原文给的建议是"去掉术语"，全篇没谈"挑选话题"，topics 虽在前文出现过（如 read about the same topics），但从未作为给科学家的建议，属未提及。 
 B) 答非所问 B 说要 Stimulate their interest.（激发兴趣）。原文确实提到术语让人 less interested in science，但 Schulman 的具体建议是"去掉术语"，并未把"激发兴趣"列为要做的动作，B 是顺着"兴趣"话题编的笼统干扰。  借用原文：less interested in science 

 C) 与原文相反 C 说要 Explain all the jargon terms.（解释所有术语），盗用了原文 jargon 一词，且第 1 段还专门说过 it made no difference if the jargon terms were defined——解释/定义术语根本无效。建议是"去掉"而非"解释"，C 正好取了原文否定掉的做法，是与原文相反。  借用原文：it made no difference if the jargon terms were defined in the text

questions.prompt: What did Texas businessman Pattillo Higgins believe?
options: The local gassy hill might start a huge fire.
There was oil leakage along the Gulf Coast.
The erupting gas might endanger local children.
There were oil deposits below a local gassy hill.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Texas businessman Pattillo Higgins believe? 

 【翻译】 得克萨斯州商人帕蒂洛·希金斯相信什么? 
 A)  当地的含气山丘可能引发一场巨大的火灾。 
 B)  墨西哥湾沿岸存在石油泄漏。 
 C)  喷发的气体可能危及当地儿童。 
 D)  当地含气山丘下面有石油矿藏。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） There were oil deposits below a local gassy hill. 
 【定位】 P2 Pattillo Higgins, a disreputable local businessman, became convinced that there was oil below the gassy hill. 
 帕蒂洛·希金斯，一个名声不佳的当地商人，开始确信那座漏气的山下面有石油。 

 【信号】 信号词 became convinced 直接交代所信 。录音里 became convinced that there was oil below the gassy hill 中的 became convinced（确信）正是表达人物信念的标志词，题干问 believe，听到 convinced 这类同义表态词就锁定这句。 

 【替换】 there was oil below the gassy hill ↔ There were oil deposits below a local gassy hill oil 扩写为 oil deposits，句意不变 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 借了第一段 schoolboys would sometimes set the hill on fire 的失火画面，但那是描述男孩点火，不是 Higgins 的信念，问的是他相信什么，答非所问。  借用原文：schoolboys would sometimes set the hill on fire 

 B) 偷换概念 B 说 oil leakage（漏油）发生在海湾沿岸，但录音是 Higgins 确信油 below the gassy hill（埋在山下），是埋藏不是泄漏；且漏出来的是气不是油，对象与状态都改了。  借用原文：there was oil below the gassy hill 

 C) 过度推断 C 说 erupting gas 可能危及当地儿童，录音第一段只提到 schoolboys would sometimes set the hill on fire，是男孩主动点火，从没说气体会危及他们，属无中生有。  借用原文：schoolboys would sometimes set the hill on fire

questions.prompt: What prevented Higgins' workers from digging a proper hole to get the oil?
options: The massive gas underground.
Their lack of the needed skill.
The sand under the hill.
Their lack of suitable tools.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What prevented Higgins' workers from digging a proper hole to get the oil? 

 【翻译】 是什么阻止了希金斯的工人挖出合适的孔洞来获取石油? 
 A)  地下大量的气体。 
 B)  他们缺乏所需的技能。 
 C)  山丘下的沙子。 
 D)  他们缺乏合适的工具。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The sand under the hill. 
 【定位】 P2 The sand under the hill defeated several attempts by Higgins' workers to make a proper hole. 
 山下的沙子让希金斯的工人们好几次想挖出一个像样的洞都以失败告终。 

 【信号】 信号词 defeated 标出受阻原因 。The sand under the hill defeated several attempts 里 defeated（挫败）正对题干的 prevented，主语 The sand under the hill 就是那个让挖洞失败的障碍，听到表挫败、阻挡的动词就锁其主语。 

 【替换】 The sand under the hill ↔ The sand under the hill. 原句主语原样搬入选项 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 The massive gas underground.，录音确实反复讲 gas（漏气的山），但让挖洞失败的是 sand 不是 gas，气体只是山的特征，盗用耳熟的 gas 来骗选。  借用原文：gas leakage was so noticeable 

 B) 未提及 B 说工人 lack of the needed skill（缺技术），录音只说沙子让他们多次失败，从没说是工人技术不行，把客观障碍换成人为不足，属无中生有。 
 D) 未提及 D 说 lack of suitable tools（缺合适工具），录音只字未提工具问题，障碍始终是山下的沙子，同样是凭想象补出的人为原因。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about Captain Lucas' drilling method?
options: It rendered many oil workers jobless.
It was not as effective as he claimed.
It gave birth to the oil drilling industry.
It was not popularized until years later.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about Captain Lucas' drilling method? 

 【翻译】 文章关于卢卡斯船长的钻探方法说了什么? 
 A)  它使许多石油工人失业。 
 B)  它并不像他声称的那样有效。 
 C)  它催生了石油钻探业。 
 D)  直到数年后它才得以推广。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It gave birth to the oil drilling industry. 
 【定位】 P3 After encountering several setbacks, Captain Lucas decided to use a drill, and his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry. 
 在遭遇几次挫折后，卢卡斯上尉决定改用钻机，他的革新开创了现代石油钻探业。 

 【信号】 信号词 created 点出方法的成果 。his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry 里 created（开创）直接交代这套方法的历史成果，问 say about method 时，听到这种交代成果、影响的动词就锁定该句。 

 【替换】 his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry ↔ It gave birth to the oil drilling industry. created 同义替换为 gave birth to 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 A 说该方法 rendered many oil workers jobless（使许多石油工人失业），录音只说它开创了钻探业，从没提失业，凭对新技术抢饭碗的常识联想出来，原文无据。 
 B) 与原文相反 B 说 It was not as effective as he claimed.（不如他宣称的有效），录音对该方法是正面肯定 his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry，B 把肯定改成否定质疑，极性相反。  借用原文：his innovations created the modern oil drilling industry 

 D) 未提及 D 说 It was not popularized until years later.（多年后才普及），录音只讲该法当即开创了行业，没说推广被推迟，时间信息属虚构。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Texas oil industry boom?
options: It radically transformed the state's economy.
It resulted in an oil surplus all over the world.
It totally destroyed the state's rural landscape.
It ruined the state's cotton and beef industries.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about Texas oil industry boom? 

 【翻译】 关于得克萨斯州石油工业繁荣我们了解到什么? 
 A)  它彻底改变了该州的经济。 
 B)  它导致全世界石油过剩。 
 C)  它彻底破坏了该州的乡村景观。 
 D)  它毁掉了该州的棉花和牛肉产业。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It radically transformed the state's economy. 
 【定位】 P5 In those days, Texas was almost entirely rural, with no large cities and practically no industry; cotton and beef were the foundation of the economy. Higgins' well changed that. 
 那时候，德州几乎全是乡村，没有大城市、几乎没有工业，棉花和牛肉是经济的支柱。希金斯的油井改变了这一切。 

 【信号】 转折信号 changed that 是结论落点 。录音先铺垫德州 almost entirely rural 的旧貌，紧接一句 Higgins' well changed that，changed that（改变了这一切）是从旧貌转向新局的转折落点，答案就在这一转之后，听到 changed that 即锁定。 

 【替换】 Texas was almost entirely rural, with no large cities and practically no industry; cotton and beef were the foundation of the economy. Higgins' well changed that ↔ It radically transformed the state's economy. 从农业旧貌到 changed that 概括为彻底改变经济 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 说造成 oil surplus all over the world（全世界石油过剩），录音只说 the sudden surplus of petroleum was not entirely a blessing for Texas，过剩是德州本地的事，B 盗用 surplus 一词却把范围放大到全世界，范围被夸大。  借用原文：the sudden surplus of petroleum was not entirely a blessing for Texas 

 C) 过度推断 C 说 totally destroyed the state's rural landscape（彻底毁掉乡村景观），录音确实说德州曾 almost entirely rural，但只讲经济被改变，从没说乡村景观被毁，盗用 rural 一词加 totally 夸大。  借用原文：Texas was almost entirely rural 

 D) 偷换概念 D 说 ruined the state's cotton and beef industries（毁掉棉花和牛肉业），录音里 cotton and beef were the foundation of the economy 是讲它们曾是旧支柱、后被石油经济取代，并未说被毁掉，盗用 cotton and beef 偷换成 ruined。  借用原文：cotton and beef were the foundation of the economy
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn about Texas' oil industry boom?

questions.prompt: What is a primary cause of employee dissatisfaction according to recent research?
options: Unsuitable jobs.
Bad managers.
Insufficient motivation.
Tough regulations.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is a primary cause of employee dissatisfaction according to recent research? 

 【翻译】 根据近期研究，员工不满的主要原因是什么？ 
 A)  不合适的工作。 
 B)  糟糕的管理者。 
 C)  动力不足。 
 D)  严苛的规章制度。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Bad managers. 
 【定位】 P1 A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that many believe they have terrible managers. 
 据最新研究，员工不满的一个主要原因是，许多人认为自己摊上了糟糕的管理者。 

 【信号】 题干原话几乎照搬的点题句 。录音开篇第二句就用 A primary cause of employee dissatisfaction, according to fresh research, is that…，与题干 a primary cause of employee dissatisfaction according to recent research 几乎逐词对应——这种「题干就是录音句的复述」是最强的答案句信号，is that 之后的内容即答案。 

 【替换】 they have terrible managers ↔ Bad managers. terrible 同义改写为 bad 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Unsuitable jobs.（不合适的岗位）录音通篇未提，整段都在讲管理者的问题，从没说员工不满是因为岗位不对口，属凭常识自行脑补的归因。 
 C) 原词陷阱 Insufficient motivation.（动力不足）看似呼应录音后文谈管理者「缺乏 drive（干劲）」的描述，但那是在说坏管理者的个人特征（第 4 段），不是员工不满的主因；它把「动力」这个似曾相识的概念安到了错误的问题上。  借用原文：those without drive 

 D) 答非所问 Tough regulations.（严苛的规章）勉强能让人联想到第 3 段的 toxic 工作环境，但录音从未把「规章严苛」列为员工不满的主因；本题问的是开篇点明的 primary cause，规章既非原话、也非主因。
questions.spoken_text: What is a primary cause of employee dissatisfaction according to recent research?

questions.prompt: What is one of the causes for poor management practices?
options: Ineffective training.
Toxic company culture.
Lack of regular evaluation.
Overburdening of managers.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is one of the causes for poor management practices? 

 【翻译】 管理实践不佳的原因之一是什么？ 
 A)  培训无效。 
 B)  有害的公司文化。 
 C)  缺乏定期评估。 
 D)  管理者负担过重。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Toxic company culture. 
 【定位】 P3 The first cause was company culture, which was seen by employees as enabling poor management practices. It was specifically stressful work environments, minimal training and a lack of accountability that were found to be the most blameworthy. Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic. 
 第一个成因是公司文化，员工认为它纵容了差劲的管理做法。具体而言，最该受责备的是充满压力的工作环境、极少的培训和缺乏问责制。这样的职场有时被形容为「有毒的」。 

 【信号】 分点信号 The first cause + 收尾点出 toxic 。录音用 The first cause was company culture 起头明确这是分点罗列的第一条成因，又在段末用 Such workplaces are sometimes described as toxic. 把这种公司文化点名为 toxic（有毒的）——首句立题、末句给出关键词，前后夹住的就是答案句。 

 【替换】 The first cause was company culture ↔ Toxic company culture. company culture 原词 + toxic 由原文回收 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Ineffective training.（无效的培训）盗用了录音 minimal training（极少的培训）里的 training 一词来勾人，但录音说的是培训「太少」，不是培训「无效」；况且 minimal training 只是 company culture 这条大成因下的一个细节，本身不是独立成因。  借用原文：minimal training 

 C) 偷换概念 Lack of regular evaluation.（缺少定期评估）借用了录音 a lack of accountability（缺乏问责）的 lack of 句式来制造耳熟感，但 accountability（问责）≠ evaluation（评估），录音从未说缺少「定期评估」；这是把一个近形概念偷换进来。  借用原文：a lack of accountability 

 D) 未提及 Overburdening of managers.（管理者负担过重）听起来像在替管理者开脱，但录音四条成因（公司文化、管理者性格、资历不足、靠资历晋升）里没有一条说管理者「负担过重」，纯属未提及。
questions.spoken_text: What is one of the causes for poor management practices?

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the study on job dissatisfaction?
options: It collected feedback from both employers and employees.
It was conducted from frontline managers' point of view.
It provided meaningful clues to solving the problem.
It was based only on the perspective of employees.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the study on job dissatisfaction? 

 【翻译】 关于工作不满研究我们了解到什么？ 
 A)  它收集了雇主和员工双方的反馈。 
 B)  它是从一线管理者的角度进行的。 
 C)  它为解决问题提供了有意义的线索。 
 D)  它仅基于员工的视角。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It was based only on the perspective of employees. 
 【定位】 P7 A point worth making is that the study was based only on the perspective of employees. The researchers didn't ask senior leaders what they thought of their frontline managers. 
 有一点值得说明：这项研究仅仅基于员工的视角。研究者并没有去问高层领导他们如何看待自己手下的一线管理者。 

 【信号】 结尾提示语 A point worth making + only 。录音末段用 A point worth making is that…（有一点值得说明）这种「特意提醒」的强调语引出关键句，后面紧跟 the study was based only on the perspective of employees，only 一词锁死研究的取材范围——结尾的特意强调语就是答案句信号。 

 【替换】 the study was based only on the perspective of employees ↔ It was based only on the perspective of employees. 几乎逐词对应的复述 
 The researchers didn't ask senior leaders ↔ only on the perspective of employees 否定句从反面印证 only 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 It collected feedback from both employers and employees.（向雇主和雇员双方收集反馈）盗用了录音里真实出现的 employees 一词，却把范围从「只问员工」夸成「双方都问」；录音明说 The researchers didn't ask senior leaders，恰恰否定了 both。  借用原文：the study was based only on the perspective of employees 

 B) 张冠李戴 It was conducted from frontline managers' point of view.（研究从一线管理者的视角进行）搬来了录音 their frontline managers 这个原词，但录音说研究是从员工视角做的，frontline managers 是被评价的对象、不是研究的视角；选项把视角张冠李戴了。  借用原文：what they thought of their frontline managers 

 C) 过度推断 It provided meaningful clues to solving the problem.（研究为解决问题提供了有价值的线索）是一句听起来很顺、很积极的评价，但末段只交代研究的取材局限（只问员工、高层没问），从没说它给出了「解决问题的有价值线索」，属凭常识脑补的拔高。
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn about the study on job dissatisfaction?

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the mining industry in Western Australia?
options: It is seeing an automation revolution.
It is bringing prosperity to the region.
It is yielding an unprecedented profit.
It is expanding at an accelerating speed.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about the mining industry in Western Australia? 

 【翻译】 文章关于西澳大利亚采矿业说了什么? 
 A)  该地区正在经历一场自动化革命。 
 B)  该地区正在给这个地区带来繁荣。 
 C)  该地区正在产生前所未有的利润。 
 D)  该地区正在以加速的速度扩张。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It is seeing an automation revolution. 
 【定位】 P1 With the use of driverless vehicles seemingly inevitable, mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are definitely taking the lead. 
 在无人驾驶车辆的使用看似不可避免的背景下，澳大利亚西部这个辽阔沙漠州的矿业公司无疑正走在前列。 

 【信号】 开头点题的总括句 。篇章独白的总判断常落在开头：录音第一句 mining companies in the vast Australian desert state of Western Australia are definitely taking the lead 直接给出西澳矿业的整体定位——在自动化（无人驾驶车辆）上领先，这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 driverless vehicles ↔ automation 无人驾驶=自动化的同义改写 
 taking the lead ↔ revolution 领先变革=同主题呼应 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 选项 bringing prosperity to the region 借用了录音里反复出现的地域词（desert state、remote communities）制造熟悉感，但录音第一句讲的是该矿业领先于自动化，并未说它给地区带来繁荣，属听到地域词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：the area's remoteness 

 C) 未提及 选项 yielding an unprecedented profit 听上去与矿业赚钱顺理成章，但录音开头讲的是技术领先，全文只提到 financial imperatives、more productive 这类追求效率的动因，从未说产出空前利润，属未提及。 
 D) 偷换概念 选项 expanding at an accelerating speed 蹭了录音里 taking the lead、a technological leap 的进取气势，但录音说的是矿业在自动化技术上领先、是技术跃进，而非整个行业在加速扩张规模，把技术领先偷换成了规模扩张。  借用原文：They are a technological leap
questions.spoken_text: What does the passage say about the mining industry in Western Australia?

questions.prompt: What is the impact of the digitization of the mining industry?
options: It exhausts resources sooner.
It creates a lot of new jobs.
It causes conflicts between employers and employees.
It calls for the retraining of unskilled mining workers.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the impact of the digitization of the mining industry? 

 【翻译】 采矿业数字化的影响是什么? 
 A)  它更快地耗尽资源。 
 B)  它创造了大量新工作岗位。 
 C)  它导致雇主与雇员之间的冲突。 
 D)  它要求对非熟练矿工进行再培训。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It creates a lot of new jobs. 
 【定位】 P6 The automation and digitization of the industry are creating a need for different jobs. These include data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence. 
 这个行业的自动化与数字化正在催生对不同岗位的需求。这些岗位包括数据科学家以及自动化和人工智能领域的工程师。 

 【信号】 因果动词 creating 引出影响 。录音第 6 段 The automation and digitization of the industry are creating a need for different jobs 用 creating a need for 直接点出数字化的后果是催生新岗位，正对题干所问的 impact，是答案句。 

 【替换】 creating a need for different jobs ↔ creates a lot of new jobs 催生岗位需求=创造新岗位 
 data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence ↔ a lot of new jobs 举例的具体岗位=新岗位的实证 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 选项 exhausts resources sooner 借矿业必然涉及资源的常识制造合理感，但录音通篇讲数字化带来岗位变化与可持续，从未说它更快耗尽资源，原文无此判断。 
 C) 原词陷阱 选项 conflicts between employers and employees 蹭了录音里 employees、workers' unions 这些词，但录音讲工会有保留是出于对偏远社区的担忧，并未说数字化在劳资双方间引发冲突，把工会的保留偷换成了劳资对立。  借用原文：Workers' unions have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology 

 D) 偷换概念 选项 retraining of unskilled mining workers 借用了录音里的 mining、workers，但录音说数字化需要的是数据科学家、工程师这类新型人才，并未提对非技术矿工的再培训，把催生新岗位偷换成了再培训旧工人。  借用原文：data scientists and engineers in automation and artificial intelligence
questions.spoken_text: What is the impact of the digitization of the mining industry?

questions.prompt: What is the attitude of workers' unions towards the introduction of new technology?
options: They welcome it with open arms.
They will wait to see its effect.
They are strongly opposed to it.
They accept it with reservations.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the attitude of workers' unions towards the introduction of new technology? 

 【翻译】 工会对引入新技术的态度是什么? 
 A)  他们张开双臂欢迎它。 
 B)  他们将等待观察它的效果。 
 C)  他们强烈反对它。 
 D)  他们有保留地接受它。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） They accept it with reservations. 
 【定位】 P7 Workers' unions have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology. But they still have reservations about the rise of automation technology. 
 工会已经接受了引入新技术不可避免这一现实。但他们对自动化技术的兴起仍有保留意见。 

 【信号】 转折 But 后才是真态度 。录音先说工会 accepted（接受），紧接 But they still have reservations 用 But 转出真态度——仍有保留。态度题的落点在转折之后，前半的接受只是铺垫。 

 【替换】 have accepted the inevitability ↔ accept it 接受=accept，态度同向 
 still have reservations ↔ with reservations 仍有保留=with reservations 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 选项 welcome it with open arms 把工会的态度拔高成热烈欢迎，只接住了 But 前的 accepted，丢了 But 后的 reservations，态度偏正、过头了。  借用原文：have accepted the inevitability of the introduction of new technology 

 B) 原词陷阱 选项 wait to see its effect 借用了录音里讲影响（impact、effect）的语境制造熟悉感，但录音说工会已经接受、只是有保留，并非按兵不动地观望效果，原文无观望此意。  借用原文：the most significant impact of robotic technology 

 C) 与原文相反 选项 strongly opposed to it 抓住录音里 reservations、main concern 的负面情绪，把有保留放大成强烈反对，但工会明说已经 accepted，并未反对，态度极性反了。  借用原文：they still have reservations about the rise of automation technology
questions.spoken_text: What is the attitude of workers unions towards the introduction of new technology?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about traffic accidents in Thailand?
options: Their cost to the nation's economy is incalculable.
They kill more people than any infectious disease.
Their annual death rate is about twice that of the global average.
They have experienced a gradual decline since the year of 2017.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about traffic accidents in Thailand? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于泰国交通事故说了什么? 
 A)  它们对国家经济造成的损失无法估量。 
 B)  它们造成的死亡人数超过任何传染病。 
 C)  它们的年死亡率约为全球平均水平的两倍。 
 D)  自2017年以来它们经历了逐渐下降。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Their annual death rate is about twice that of the global average. 
 【定位】 P1 According to official statistics, Thailand's annual road-death rate is almost double the global average. 
 据官方统计，泰国的年度道路死亡率几乎是全球平均水平的两倍。 

 【信号】 地名加数字即落点 。第一段开门见山点出 Thailand's annual road-death rate is almost double the global average，地名 Thailand 加上倍数 double 同时出现，正是预读时盯的两个锚点，这一句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 almost double the global average ↔ about twice that of the global average double 同义于 twice 
 Thailand's annual road-death rate ↔ Their annual death rate 代词回指加省略 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Their cost to the nation's economy is incalculable. 谈经济成本不可估量，录音第一段只说死亡率高、并说这本可改变，从未提及对经济的成本，属凭常识脑补的无中生有。 
 B) 张冠李戴 They kill more people than any infectious disease. 里的 infectious disease 确实在录音出现，但那是第二段讲全球情况 road accidents kill more people every year than any infectious disease，主语是 Globally 而非泰国，被错安到了泰国头上。  借用原文：road accidents kill more people every year than any infectious disease 

 D) 与原文相反 They have experienced a gradual decline since the year of 2017 说泰国死亡率自 2017 年逐渐下降，2017 这个年份录音第二段 the death toll in 2017 确实念到，但那是全球死亡人数的统计年份，且原文说泰国道路危险本可改变、并无下降之说，极性正好相反。  借用原文：the death toll in 2017
questions.spoken_text: What does the speaker say about traffic accidents in Thailand?

questions.prompt: What do we learn from an American institute's statistics regarding road deaths?
options: They show a difference between rich and poor nations.
They don't reflect the changes in individual countries.
They rise and fall from year to year.
They are not as reliable as claimed.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from an American institute's statistics regarding road deaths? 

 【翻译】 从一家美国研究机构关于道路死亡的统计数据中我们了解到什么? 
 A)  它们显示了富国和穷国之间的差异。 
 B)  它们没有反映各个国家的变化。 
 C)  它们每年都有起伏。 
 D)  它们并不像声称的那样可靠。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They don't reflect the changes in individual countries. 
 【定位】 P2 According to the institute, the overall number of deaths has been more or less static since the turn of the century. But that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries. 
 据该机构称，自世纪之交以来，死亡总数大体保持平稳。但这掩盖了各个国家内部的大量变化。 

 【信号】 转折 But 后才是真意 。前半句说总数基本平稳，紧接 But that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries，转折词 But 之后才是说话人真正强调的那层意思——这组数据掩盖了个体国家的变化，正是答案落点。 

 【替换】 that disguises a lot of changes in individual countries ↔ They don't reflect the changes in individual countries. disguise 转写为 don't reflect 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 They show a difference between rich and poor nations. 说贫富差异——贫富国家的对比确在录音第三段出现 In many poor countries … In many rich countries, by contrast，但那是后文展开的内容，并非这组美国机构统计本身得出的结论，题干问的恰是这组统计，张冠李戴了。  借用原文：In many poor countries … In many rich countries, by contrast 

 C) 与原文相反 They rise and fall from year to year. 说死亡数逐年起落，恰与原文 has been more or less static since the turn of the century（大体保持平稳）相反，把平稳说成了波动。  借用原文：has been more or less static since the turn of the century 

 D) 未提及 They are not as reliable as claimed. 质疑这组美国机构统计的可靠性，但录音对这组数据只说它平稳、它掩盖了各国变化，从未说它不可靠（说统计不充分的是第三段的穷国官方统计，非这组）。
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn from an American Institute's statistics regarding road deaths?

questions.prompt: What is said about middle-income countries?
options: Many of them have increasing numbers of cars on the road.
Many of them are following the example set by Thailand.
Many of them have seen a decline in road-death rates.
Many of them are investing heavily in infrastructure.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is said about middle-income countries? 

 【翻译】 关于中等收入国家说了什么? 
 A)  它们中的许多国家道路上的汽车数量在增加。 
 B)  它们中的许多国家正在效仿泰国树立的榜样。 
 C)  它们中的许多国家道路死亡率出现了下降。 
 D)  它们中的许多国家正在基础设施方面进行大量投资。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Many of them have seen a decline in road-death rates. 
 【定位】 P4 But the most important and intriguing changes are taking place in middle-income countries… According to researchers, in China and South Africa, traffic deaths have been falling since 2000, and in India since 2012, and the Philippines reached its peak four years ago. 
 但最重要也最耐人寻味的变化正发生在中等收入国家……据研究者称，在中国和南非，交通死亡数自 2000 年起持续下降，印度自 2012 年起下降，菲律宾在四年前达到峰值。 

 【信号】 群体名加并列实例 。第四段点出 middle-income countries 后，立即用 China、South Africa、India、Philippines 一连串实例说明 traffic deaths have been falling，群体名加并列例证处即答案句。 

 【替换】 traffic deaths have been falling since 2000 ↔ Many of them have seen a decline in road-death rates. falling 名词化为 a decline 
 in China and South Africa … in India … the Philippines ↔ Many of them 多国列举概括为 Many of them 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 Many of them have increasing numbers of cars on the road. 说车辆增多，increasing 与车确在录音出现，但那是第三段讲穷国 a fast-growing fleet of cars and motorbikes，说的是低收入国家而非中等收入国家，主体错位。  借用原文：a fast-growing fleet of cars and motorbikes 

 B) 与原文相反 Many of them are following the example set by Thailand. 说这些国家效仿泰国，可原文恰恰相反——whether Thailand can soon follow suit，是问泰国能否效仿这些国家，方向被颠倒了。  借用原文：whether Thailand can soon follow suit 

 D) 原词陷阱 Many of them are investing heavily in infrastructure. 里的 infrastructure 确在录音末段出现 not just in better infrastructure，但那是讲解决办法、且说光靠基建不够，根本没说中等收入国家在大举投资基建，属原词陷阱式的答非所问。  借用原文：not just in better infrastructure

questions.explanation:
【题目】 What else could be done to reduce fatal road accidents in addition to safer roads? 

 【翻译】 除了更安全的道路之外,还可以做什么来减少致命的道路事故? 
 A)  培养更好的驾驶行为。 
 B)  为驾驶员提供更好的培训。 
 C)  废除所有过时的交通规则。 
 D)  对超速施加更重的处罚。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Foster better driving behavior. 
 【定位】 P6 The solution lies not just in better infrastructure, but in better social incentives. Safe driving habits are practices which people know they should follow but often don't. People respond to incentives, such as traffic laws that are actually enforced. 
 解决之道不只在于更好的基础设施，更在于更好的社会激励。安全驾驶是人们明知该做却常常不做的事。人们会对激励作出反应，比如真正得到执行的交通法规。 

 【信号】 提对策句 solution lies in 。末段直接给方案 The solution lies not just in better infrastructure, but in better social incentives，The solution lies in 是典型的提对策信号，紧接着 Safe driving habits 把社会激励落到培养安全驾驶习惯，这一串就是答案句。 

 【替换】 better social incentives ↔ Foster better driving behavior. 概念落地的同义改写 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 Provide better training for drivers. 说给司机更好的培训，听上去很对症，但录音只说要靠社会激励养成习惯，从未提到培训 driver，属凭常识脑补。 
 C) 与原文相反 Abolish all outdated traffic rules. 里的 traffic 与法规确呼应录音 traffic laws that are actually enforced，但原文是要让交通法规真正得到执行，选项却说废除过时规则，方向相反，且 all、outdated 更是无中生有的绝对化。  借用原文：traffic laws that are actually enforced 

 D) 过度推断 Impose heavier penalties on speeding. 顺着 traffic laws that are actually enforced 的执法语境联想出加重处罚、罚超速，可原文只说让法规真正被执行，既没说加重 penalties，也没专门提 speeding，属过度推断。  借用原文：traffic laws that are actually enforced
